question: What is the main job of the testes in the male reproductive system?
explanation: Spot on! The testes are the primary male organs responsible for making both testosterone (the male hormone) and sperm cells. You've got this! [learn more](GNS311_U1_T8#GNS311_U1_T8_h1)

question: Why do the testes hang outside the main body cavity in the scrotum?

options.A: To shorten the length of the vas deferens tube
options.B: To allow easier passage of urine through the urethra
options.C: To protect the internal organs from high abdominal pressure
options.D: To keep sperm production at a slightly lower temperature

explanation: Brilliant! Sperm cells need a temperature slightly cooler than normal body heat to develop properly. The hanging scrotum acts like a natural cooling system. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T8#GNS311_U1_T8_h1)

question: Which hormone tells the Leydig cells in the testes to start producing testosterone?
explanation: Correct! Luteinizing hormone (LH) is released from the brain and travels down to target the Leydig cells, telling them to pump out testosterone. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T8#GNS311_U1_T8_h2)

question: What is the main job of Sertoli cells while sperm is being made?

options.A: Supporting and nourishing the developing sperm cells
options.B: Producing the alkaline fluid found in semen
options.C: Releasing gonadotropin-releasing hormone into the blood
options.D: Carrying mature sperm through the vas deferens

explanation: You got it! Think of Sertoli cells as the 'nurse' cells of the testes—they look after the baby sperm cells and give them food and support while they grow. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T8#GNS311_U1_T8_h2)

question: What triggers the physical changes of puberty in teenage boys?

options.A: A sudden drop in core body temperature
options.B: A sudden surge in testosterone and related hormones
options.C: The full closure of the growth plates in long bones
options.D: An increase in the production of red blood cells

explanation: Spot on! A sudden rise in testosterone kicks off all those classic changes we see during adolescent growth. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T8#GNS311_U1_T8_h3)

question: A teenage boy asks why his voice is cracking and getting deeper. What is the cause?

options.A: Weakening of the throat muscles during physical exercise
options.B: Temporary irritation of the airway from rapid lung growth
options.C: Growth and thickening of the vocal cords due to testosterone
options.D: Swelling of the tonsils caused by common adolescent infections

explanation: Correct! As testosterone levels rise, the larynx and vocal cords grow larger and thicker, which naturally drops the pitch of the voice. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T8#GNS311_U1_T8_h3)

question: Which part of the nervous system is responsible for triggering a penile erection?
explanation: Well done! The parasympathetic nervous system handles the 'rest and digest' actions, including sending signals that relax blood vessels so erectile tissue can fill with blood. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T8#GNS311_U1_T8_h4)

question: What is the main difference between emission and ejaculation?

options.A: Emission is controlled by parasympathetic nerves, while erection is sympathetic
options.B: Emission involves only the testes, while ejaculation involves the prostate
options.C: Emission moves fluid into the urethra, while ejaculation expels it outward
options.D: Emission happens before puberty, while ejaculation occurs only in adulthood

explanation: Spot on! Emission gathers and moves the fluid into the upper urethra, while ejaculation uses muscle contractions to push it completely out of the body. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T8#GNS311_U1_T8_h4)

question: How does male andropause usually differ from female menopause?

options.A: It involves a slow and gradual decline in hormone levels
options.B: It causes an immediate and complete stop to all sperm production
options.C: It affects every single man at exactly age fifty years
options.D: It occurs during early adolescence rather than late adulthood

explanation: Correct! Unlike the quicker hormone drop in female menopause, men experience a very gradual, slow decrease in hormone levels as they age. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T8#GNS311_U1_T8_h5)

question: What is a common physical change that happens to the prostate gland as men age?

options.A: Total loss of the ability to produce seminal fluid
options.B: Complete shrinkage of the glandular tissue
options.C: Development of chronic bacterial infections in all men
options.D: Gradual enlargement that can affect urinary flow

explanation: You got it! The prostate tends to grow larger with age, which can sometimes press against the urethra and make urinating a bit tricky. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T8#GNS311_U1_T8_h5)

question: What is the most important first step when doing a sensitive reproductive health assessment?

options.A: Focusing solely on laboratory test results rather than patient words
options.B: Involving family members in every part of the interview process
options.C: Establishing a trusting and professional rapport to reduce anxiety
options.D: Immediately beginning the physical examination without asking questions

explanation: Spot on! Because talking about reproductive health can feel awkward or scary for patients, building trust first makes them feel safe enough to share the truth. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T8#GNS311_U1_T8_h6)

question: A male patient says he has noticed sexual changes after starting a new heart medication. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Review his medication list to check for known side effects
options.B: Tell him to stop taking all his heart tablets immediately
options.C: Refer him directly for specialized surgical intervention
options.D: Reassure him that all prescription drugs have zero sexual impact

explanation: Correct! Many heart medications are famous for causing sexual side effects. Checking his drug list is a smart and logical first nursing action. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T8#GNS311_U1_T8_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a good lifestyle habit for supporting male reproductive health?

options.A: Smoking cigarettes regularly to stimulate circulation
options.B: Engaging in regular physical exercise routines
options.D: Maintaining a healthy body weight through balanced diet

explanation: You nailed it! Smoking actually harms your blood vessels, ruining the good circulation needed for proper reproductive health. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T8#GNS311_U1_T8_h7)

question: Why should young adult men learn to do regular testicular self-examinations?

options.A: It helps detect lumps or changes early when treatment is most effective
options.B: It stops the development of benign prostatic hyperplasia later in life
options.C: It guarantees complete protection against sexually transmitted infections
options.D: It prevents the normal age-related decline in testosterone levels

explanation: Brilliant! Just like breast self-exams for women, checking early helps catch unusual lumps or changes when treatment works best. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T8#GNS311_U1_T8_h7)
